Projects

Nike iOS App and Release Automation

This summer I worked as an iOS Software Engineering Intern on Nike's Mobile Foundation team, where I built, debugged, and shipped feature updates in the Nike app's codebase. I worked with engineers and QA through JIRA and helped automate downstream processes like testing. I designed and built an AI-assisted release automation system using Cursor that runs the weekly release candidate cuts by connecting Fastlane, Jenkins, GitHub tagging, and Slack notifications, which reduced manual release steps. Along the way I grew my mobile development skills, AI skills, and understanding of workflows in a corporate setting.

Tools: Swift, Xcode, Cursor, Fastlane, Jenkins, GitHub, JIRA, Slack

Emory's Hackathon Operations

Emory Hacks is a 36-hour hackathon hosted at Emory University that aims to bring hundreds of students together to build projects. As part of the operations team, I manage and coordinate operations, including sponsorship recruitment, day-of event logistics, and cross-team coordination. I also help run the judging: I recruit and onboard judges, develop the evaluation rubrics, and streamline communication between judges, participants, and team members so the evaluation is fair and efficient. On top of that, I do more development work and coordinate between the tech designers and graphic designers, as well as with the coordination leads. I helped with the event website too.

Visit the Emory Hacks 2025 site

Vowel Counter in MIPS Assembly

I wrote a MIPS assembly program that counts the vowels in a large text file. It reads the file in chunks of 4,096 characters, so it can handle something as long as a full book. Each chunk goes through a counting function that treats capital and lowercase letters the same, and the program adds up the total and prints it. The idea came from a linguistics class about the role of vowels in language, which made me curious how many vowels show up in a 300-page book.

Language: MIPS assembly
